correctness.rationale: Sorting is continuous piecewise linear, with every permutation matrix realized on a full-dimensional strict-order chamber. The global two-input seminorm Lipschitz factor equals the maximum induced variation norm of these permutation matrices; telescoping over single step functions H_k yields max_k B_k(w)/w_k, with exact strict-chamber witnesses. For sine weights, a centered alternating minority block attains the sum of the 2min(k,n-k) largest weights; elementary finite sine sums yield B_k(v)=Lambda_n v_k for every k, including even central case. A nonnegative central-block matrix A whose rows are averages of realizable cut indicators obeys A w <= B(w), has positive center column and a central row of all ones, hence is irreducible. The positive sine vector is its Perron eigenvector with eigenvalue Lambda_n; multiplication by the positive left Perron eigenvector proves the universal lower bound, and equality plus simplicity forces w proportional to v. Independent brute enumeration of all binary cuts for n=2..10 reproduced every target level ratio; exact proof covers all n.

source_inspections.title: Sine-edge weights uniquely minimize the two-input variation instability of finite sorting

value.rationale: Choosing edge weights to minimize the global two-input sorting instability is a natural stable-metric design problem, distinct from the classical one-input energy rearrangement question. The unique sine profile, exact parity effect and asymptotic 2/pi improvement over uniform edge weights constitute a mathematically motivated sharp optimization and rigidity theorem.

final_claim: For n>=2, increasing sorting of real n-vectors has exact two-input common-positive-path-weight variation modulus max_{1<=k<n} B_k(w)/w_k. The unique optimal positive path-edge weights up to scale are sin(j*pi/n), with minimum cot(pi/(2n)) if n even and csc(pi/(2n)) if n odd. The uniform-weight factor is n-1.
limitations: Another weighted rearrangement or nonlinear Collatz–Wielandt text might implicitly contain the optimized sine formula under a different operator name.
